messages:
maria.g: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to introduce a 'soft-defer' composition step for policy evals. Current deterministic ordering is causing periodic cost spikes when many tenants prefer the same cheap region. Idea: let evaluators return (score, defer_level) where defer_level ∈ {hard, soft, hint} and the compositor applies a small random jitter + penalty if many soft-defer choices collide.

kevin: can you sketch what the return shape looks like? and how this wouldn't violate SLOs for latency-sensitive tenants?

maria.g: sketch below — short version: latency policies mark hard/hint; cost policies are soft by default. compositor folds scores like: normalized_score = base_score + lambda_defer[defer_level] + jitter(seed=tenant_id, window=1s). jitter is tiny (~1-3ms equivalent converted to score). This biases away from synchronized picks without blocking hard constraints.

sam: curious about tie-breakers across regions — if two regions have same normalized_score but different cold-gpu cost, do we prefer warm but expensive?

maria.g: prefer warm GPUs (affinity) if latency weight > threshold, else cost wins. Suggest adding a small affinity_bonus per region if tenant has recent cache hits: affinity_bonus = min(0.2, recent_prefix_hits / 100). This keeps cache-friendly routing.

anya: how does this interact with hedged requests/duplicates? we don't want jitter to cause lots of hedging.

maria.g: hedging stays orthogonal — compositor exposes a 'confidence' scalar derived from score gap to best option. hedging only triggers if confidence < hedging_threshold. Jitter reduces confidence only when options are within tight band; that recovers cost distribution while keeping hedges rare.

kevin: implementation concerns: policy DSL currently returns float score only. We'll need to change DSL ext and update adapters. That could be a breaking change for many plugins. propose an adapter shim: if policy returns float, treat as (score, soft). new policies can return tuple. shim keeps backwards compat.

policy-bot: note: added issue #2987 to policy-surface repo to track DSL extension and shim plan.

sam: simulation plan? we should run sim with 1k tenants, varying SLA mix and affinity distribution. measure cost variance and p50/p99 latency.

maria.g: yes — add a sim scenario: tenant_sla = {gold:20%, standard:60%, free:20%}; warm_cache_pct per tenant sampled from Beta(2,5). Run with and without soft-defer for 30m virtual time. Telemetry: route_choice_distribution, per-tenant cost, fallback rate, hedging_rate.

anya: rollout: canary in non-prod region first, then 5% production traffic by user_id hash, ensure metric alerts on p99 latency + cost-per-token delta > 10%.

kevin: infra notes: need route-compat cache invalidation hook — when compositor policy logic changes, cached decisions must be stamped. otherwise stale cache will nullify soft-defer effects. infra-bot can help with a TTL bump.

infra-bot: recall: cache TTLs default 60s. plan: bump to 10s for canary and add cache-version header to decisions so we can invalidate globally.

maria.g: open questions: 1) what lambda_defer values (soft penalty) map to meaningful cost balancing without harming latency? 2) how to surface explainability (why route chosen) for SRE/debugging?

kevin: for (1) we should start lambda_soft = 0.1 (score units equivalent to ~2ms), lambda_hint = 0.02. tune in sim.

sam: for explainability, compositor will emit decision_explain: [top3 {route, raw_score, defer_level, affinity_bonus}]. keep in trace sample.

anya: nit: ensure we don't leak tenant-sensitive telemetry cross-tenant — redact tenant ids in public dashboards.

maria.g: next steps I can take: PR for DSL shim + tests, sim config, and a 2-week experiment run. tagging kevin for impl and infra-bot for TTL changes. Any objections?

kevin: no objections. will start a branch after the issue lands.

sam: +1. sounds reasonable.

anya: +1. please add a rollback plan for config flip.

maria.g: will add rollback (flip config, restore TTL) and a follow-up on postmortem checklist if canary shows regression. thanks all.
